title: SCIM & SSO Provisioning: Validation and Operational Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines the standardized validation, testing, and operational steps for customer SCIM provisioning and OIDC/SAML SSO integrations with Redwood Inference. It is intended for Customer Success Engineers (CSEs), Solutions Architects, and the customer's identity/IT teams. Follow this document for pre-production validation, go-live checks, troubleshooting, and post-go-live monitoring items.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to Dedicated and Private deployment customers implementing automated user provisioning (SCIM 2.0) and single sign-on (OIDC or SAML).
- Covers initial onboarding validation, periodic health checks, and playbooked escalation routes.
- Does NOT replace corporate security reviews or customer-specific legal controls; use alongside the Regulated Go‑Live Security Gates playbook.

When to use this playbook:
1. During the final phase of enterprise onboarding where users/groups are provisioned from the customer's Identity Provider (IdP).
2. When SSO authentication or SCIM provisioning errors are observed during canary or rollout.
3. When rolling out auto-provisioning to a larger user population (canary -> gradual ramp).

Prerequisites (customer and Redwood):
| Item | Required | Owner | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| SCIM base URL and bearer token | Yes | Customer + CSE | Token with sufficient scopes for user/group CRUD
| IdP metadata (SAML) or OIDC client configuration | Yes | Customer | Include certificate or JWKS URL
| Firewall rules / allowlist | Yes | Customer + Infra | IP ranges or VPC peering as documented in Private deployments guide
| Test account(s) with admin and non-admin roles | Yes | Customer | One canary user per target group
| Test group(s) mapping plan | Yes | Customer | Map IdP groups -> Redwood roles (viewer/editor/admin)

Roles and responsibilities:
- Customer Success (owner): coordination, validation checklist, go/no-go recommendation.
- Solutions Architect: review mapping strategy, permission boundaries, and any custom attributes.
- SRE/Infra (for Private deployments): ensure network connectivity, firewall/NAT, and certificate trust.
- Customer IT/IdP team: provide test environment, tokens, and perform IdP-side tests.

Validation checklist (pre-canary):
1. Verify network connectivity: from IdP to Redwood SCIM endpoint for hosted customers, or the customer's SCIM endpoint (private). Use curl from a bastion host.
   - Example: curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" "https://scim.redwood.example.com/v2/Users"
2. Confirm token scopes and expiry: run a test PUT/POST and ensure 2xx response for valid payload.
3. Schema mapping review: confirm required attributes (userName, name.givenName, name.familyName, emails[type=work]) are mapped.
4. Group sync dry-run: perform a scoped sync of 5 users and compare expected role assignments.
5. SSO smoke test: authenticate via OIDC/SAML with a test user, assert role mapping and session creation.
6. Audit logging enabled: ensure provisioning events are emitted to the customer-visible audit log (or syslog for Private).

Step-by-step canary validation (1–3 days recommended):
1. Enable auto-provisioning for a single test group with 5–10 users. Document the exact group ID and filter.
2. Run an initial full sync (customer triggers) and confirm: user create events, group assignment, and correct role attachments.
3. Perform authentication tests for each user: internal UI login, API token minting (if permitted), and session termination.
4. Introduce controlled churn: change an attribute (email or displayName) in IdP and confirm delta sync updates the user in Redwood.
5. Revoke provisioning token (simulate rotation) and verify that failures are surfaced to the CSE dashboard and to the configured alert channel.
6. Expand to 25% of the user population after successful 24–48h stability window, then to 100% after 72h of stable metrics.

Operational SLOs and KPIs to track during rollouts:
- Provisioning success rate >= 99.5% (per-hour window).
- Average SCIM API latency < 350ms for 95th percentile for individual user operations.
- SSO authentication success >= 99.0% across test samples.
- Time-to-detect provisioning failures (alert to on-call) < 5 minutes.

Sample SCIM payloads and curl examples:
- Create user (minimal payload):
  curl -X POST
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>"
    -H "Content-Type: application/json"
    https://scim.redwood.example.com/v2/Users
    -d '{"userName":"j.smith@example.com","name":{"givenName":"John","familyName":"Smith"},"emails":[{"value":"j.smith@example.com","type":"work","primary":true}],"active":true}'

- Sample OIDC client test (using oauth2-tool):
  oauth2-tool authorize --client-id <CLIENT_ID> --redirect-uri "https://app.redwood.example.com/_callback" --scope "openid email profile"

Common failure modes and troubleshooting steps:
- 401 Unauthorized from SCIM endpoints:
  1) Confirm token validity and scopes (check expiration).
  2) Confirm system time skew on IdP or Redwood gateway.
  3) Check for IP allowlist blocks.
- 400/422 on user import:
  1) Verify JSON structure against SCIM schema (common missing attributes: emails, userName).
  2) Inspect validation error in response body for attribute names.
- Duplicate user errors:
  1) Verify externalId mapping and ensure IdP and Redwood use same canonical identifier.
- Group mapping mismatches:
  1) Check case-sensitivity of group names and whitespace.
  2) Confirm that nested groups are supported/flattened according to customer's plan.

Debugging tools and logs to collect before escalation:
- SCIM request/response pairs (with sensitive fields redacted).
- IdP audit logs for the matching timestamp and user IDs.
- Application logs showing role assignment and session creation events.
- Network traces (tcpdump) for Private deployments if connectivity issues suspected.

Escalation matrix (when to escalate to Redwood SRE or Product):
- Escalate to SRE within 30 minutes if provisioning success rate < 95% after attempted remediation.
- Escalate to Product if schema or role mapping behavior appears inconsistent with product design (include sample payloads and expected vs actual).
- Contacts:
  - CSE on-call: customer-success-oncall@redwood.example.com
  - SRE Pager: +1-555-010-999 (use only for P1 affecting >50% users)
  - Product triage: product-integrations@redwood.example.com

Post-go-live monitoring and QBR metrics to report:
- Weekly: provisioning success rate, average latency, number of mapping exceptions, manual fix count.
- Monthly QBR slides should include a 90-day trend for: activated users, deprovisioned users, time-to-provision median, and incidents triggered by provisioning.

Rollout and rollback plan (canary -> full):
1. Canary: 5–10 users for 48–72 hours.
2. Ramp: 25% for 48 hours; 75% for 24 hours.
3. Full: remaining 100% after 72 hours stability.
4. Rollback: disable auto-provisioning and run a manual reconciliation to revoke recently-provisioned accounts; notify affected teams and attach incident ticket.

Security considerations and compliance notes:
- Never include cleartext tokens in shared logs; use redaction.
- Ensure audit trails are retained per the customer's retention policy (default 90 days) and documented in the compliance folder.
- For Private deployments, confirm HSM/KMS integrations for token storage.

Appendix A: Common SCIM response samples (redacted)
- Success: 201 Created with user resource including id, externalId, meta.version.
- Error: 409 Conflict with detail referencing externalId collision.

Appendix B: Quick checklist for customer-run tests (copyable)
- [ ] Obtain SCIM token and test curl against /v2/Users
- [ ] Create test user and verify created in UI within 30s
- [ ] Update attribute in IdP and confirm delta sync within 5 minutes
- [ ] Authenticate via SSO and verify role assignment
- [ ] Rotate token and confirm alerting and recovery
